rules.title: Requirements
rules.statement:
- Resource kinds may claim workspace-relative path prefixes and name an owner command.
- Match complete path segments. The longest matching prefix wins.
- Normalize relative, absolute, and file-URL links against the conversation's workspace,
  preserving source positions and the existing workspace-boundary checks.
- Pass the normalized path and conversation workspace ID to the owner command.
- Accept a resource and page, panel, or compound destination. Qualify local references
  with the owner and project, and reject foreign resources throughout page, panel,
  parent, and compound destinations.
- Open unclaimed paths and missing resources through the existing workspace flow.
  Report resolver failures when the link is opened.
- Render local links in read-only rich messages as resource bubbles. Resolve owner
  labels, icons, and page URLs without changing the stored message.
- Use the shared resource icon registry, with the resource kind's icon as the default.
  Show the icon with the resolved label. Bubbles have no tooltip or underline, including on hover.
- Keep explicit web references on the native web-opening path, with mouse and keyboard activation.
- Show web links in read-only rich messages as bubbles with the linked site's own icon, fetched by the runtime.
  Show a globe while the icon loads and when the site has none. Web links still open in a new tab or the system browser.
  See the [link icons reference](../references/architecture/0028-link-icons.md).
- Apply source positions to page destinations and every page in compound destinations
  that open a document, replacing any competing section while retaining parent navigation.
  A page that opens no document keeps the owner's destination without the position.
- Detect ordinary file paths in prose without agent-specific link formatting.
  Support Markdown links, inline-code file references, and explicit reference links too.
  Paths found in prose or inline code are guesses. Show one as a bubble only when its owner
  resolves it or the file exists in the conversation workspace; otherwise keep the text as written.
  Markdown links and explicit references stay links even when the file is missing.
  Preserve route-group parentheses and dynamic path segments; never turn a path suffix into a different file link.
  Preserve keyboard activation, web links, source positions, and editable Markdown.
- Copying a message keeps every bubble's text and formatting in both plain text and HTML.
- Keep completed bubbles stable while more text streams. Ignore late presentation
  results after a link changes or its view closes.
- Let agents invoke the same owner command through the existing command API.

rules.title: Acceptance
rules.statement:
1. Open a ticket draft link from a conversation while another workspace is selected.
   Resolve it using the conversation's workspace and open the ticket in Planner.
2. Open a saved ticket file path and select the corresponding document by its stable ID.
3. Prefer a more specific path claim and do not match a sibling directory with a similar name.
4. Open an unclaimed file through the workspace browser. Reject an outside-workspace
   path and a resolver result from another resource owner or project.
5. Share a plain ticket or saved-document path in prose and show its owner label and
   icon without requiring any link syntax. Support Markdown, inline-code, and explicit
   reference bubbles too. Activate them by keyboard and preserve ordinary web links.
   Keep text such as `origin/main`, github.com and Node.js, and paths to missing files,
   as plain text or code.
6. Stream more text without recreating earlier bubbles. Edit Markdown without
   replacing its source with resolved labels or URLs.
7. Load an independent extension's declaration through the packaged host, expose
   its qualified resolver in metadata, and invoke it through the command API.

rules.title: Custom use cases we drop or move
rules.statement:
| Existing use | Required change |
| --- | --- |
| Save a key with `set(key, value)` without keeping the revision from the editor's read. | Keep the read revision, save against it and handle a conflict. Blind replacement leaves the authoring API. |
| Let a collection generate IDs, keep ordering and attach files to items. | The extension defines stable domain IDs and ordering. The attachment helper handles metadata and retry identity. |
| Create and edit documents by file ID through `storage.files` or `ctx.files.createText`. | Store metadata and an asset reference in an owned record, or edit a file through an explicit root. New bytes create a new immutable version. Old file-ID URLs keep working (see [URLs](book.json)). |
| Open every published Artifacts revision as a permanent local HTML file. | Read its asset or explicitly export a file. Migrate direct-file consumers before removing redundant files. |

Small extensions write more code than a bare `get/set` pair: they keep revisions, handle save
outcomes and own their domain schema and ordering.

rules.title: Storage capacity
rules.statement:
The asset store keeps completed versions with no automatic expiry
([assets guide](../guides/sdk/0002-assets.md#read-and-cancel)). 0.44 ships records and assets with
that behavior: no eviction, no compaction and no enforced budgets. They stay off until the
[capacity and recovery PRD](book.json) publishes
measured defaults. That PRD's release gates block the 0.45 data conversion and any change that
turns eviction, compaction or budgets on. Do not resolve capacity by silently deleting local
durability, conflicts, published URLs or restore material.

rules.title: Attachment helper
rules.statement:
`attachments.add(parentRecordId, file, { operationId })` composes records and assets, with no new
table, byte store or queue. It ships in 0.44 with `attachments.list(parentRecordId)` and
`attachments.delete(attachmentId, { operationId })`.

- Attachment metadata lives in its own namespace inside the extension's storage owner. It never
  appears in the extension's `records.list()`.
- `add` checks that the parent record exists and is not deleted, and rejects otherwise.
- A new upload's attachment ID is derived from its operation ID. Converted blobs and collection
  attachments keep their existing IDs.
- An identical retry returns the original result. The same operation ID with a changed file, name
  or parent returns `operation_payload_changed`. An operation ID already used by a different
  operation, such as a record commit, returns `operation_id_in_use`.
- Display and download go through authorized URLs (see [URLs](book.json)). Ordering stays with the
  extension's own records.

rules.title: Save outcomes
rules.statement:
Add two members to `StorageSaveOutcome` in 0.44. Adding a union member can break exhaustive
callers, so it lands while 0.44 already breaks.

- `expired-revision`: the captured revision's base is gone. The draft stays; the caller must decide.
  Nothing returns it until compaction is enabled.
- A capacity outcome that names the space needed. Nothing returns it until budgets are enforced.

Enforcing budgets makes calls that succeed today fail, which is breaking. Turn it on only in a
breaking release after the [0010 gates](book.json) pass.

rules.statement:

([define-extension-view.ts](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/define-extension-view.ts)). They map

rules.title: Data and ownership requirements
rules.statement:
- Old and new names use the same storage owner, root rules and safe-path checks, and never create
  another writable copy. The same owner does not mean the same fallback (see `files.currentWorkspace`).
- Keep mount declarations, access grants, file-change events, view refresh, revisions, tombstones,
  conflicts and restore recovery. A local save must not report relay acceptance.
- Carry the editor's read revision through save commands. Return conflicts before starting external
  work. Retry identical storage requests; never replay commands.

rules.title: Data conversion
rules.statement:
On `main`, KV and collection rows already live in records. Since 0.46 the host starts with a new
database, so there are no old KV or collection rows to import
([ADR 0103](../adrs/0103-database-baseline-replaces-in-place-upgrades.md)).

- KV needs no data conversion. A key's record ID equals `records.id(key)` in the same scope, and the
  value is unchanged. Callers switch to `records.read` and `save`.
- Collection items are records under a separate collection namespace, with value
  `{ value, sortOrder }`. `records.list()` does not show them. Each owning extension converts them to
  domain records in a `storage.migrate` step. Keep resource IDs and ordering, and keep the meaning of
  `createIfAbsent` and `deleteIfValue` without claiming a distributed lock.
- Blob and file-ID data converts to assets plus attachment records. Keep IDs, names, media types and
  parent links. Resolve old project-wide file ownership from stored references; never give an
  ambiguous file to whichever extension reads it first.
- A 0.45 extension converts on a 0.45 host, where the collection and blob methods are gone. So 0.44
  adds a migration reader for collection records and blob metadata, reachable inside
  `storage.migrate`, and keeps it through 0.45. Core extensions use it from the published 0.44 SDK.
- Planner and Reports drafts move to `files.local` with a one-time move in their 0.45 conversion.
  See [Planner and Reports drafts](book.json).
- While an extension converts in a project, the host rejects that extension's commands, hooks and
  schedules in that project with `storage_converting`. Callers retry after conversion. Use stable
  migration operation IDs, resume interrupted conversion and verify it before admitting commands.
  Avoid ongoing dual writes.

creates a new URL while the old URL still returns the old bytes.

rules.statement:

rules.title: Client disk costs
rules.statement:
A native or hosted runtime stores its own database and assets. A second replicating runtime adds
another local store. A browser connected to a runtime has UI state and browser caching; it is not
another durable copy of the runtime's journal and asset history.

Account for all of these when measuring a runtime:

- Current record state and indexes.
- Accepted and pending operations, receipts, revision information, deletion markers and conflicts.
- Complete immutable asset versions, including historical and unresolved versions.
- Materialized editable files, exported files and local source drafts.
- Partial uploads, interrupted downloads and staging files.
- Installed packages, caches and migration backups, including temporary migration peaks.

For example, 100 distinct versions of a 10 MB asset use about **1 GB of asset bytes** before
database overhead, editable copies or temporary transfers. A one-byte change produces another full
version; the store does not encode binary differences. Identical content reuses the completed
version within the same workbench and extension owner. A separate transfer can still stage bytes
before completion. Do not assume deduplication across owners, machines or backups.

Deleting a record does not reclaim its completed assets. Project cleanup removes mutable blobs but
keeps immutable versions. An interrupted transfer keeps partial bytes for resumption. These
behaviors keep recovery safe but give no bound on client disk use.

The sync code enumerates assets from snapshot receipts as well as current records, so a new or
returning environment would fetch old versions it has not opened. Verification also reads complete
local assets. Measure disk reads, network bytes, initial sync time and reconnect cost as history
grows; current file size alone does not predict them.

rules.title: 1. Define storage classes and budgets
rules.statement:
Separate required local data from downloadable history and disposable caches. Pending operations,
unsent bytes, unsaved drafts and unresolved work stay protected. A user may pin content for offline
use. Published history can stay retained remotely without being pinned on every client. Evict a
local copy only when another verified durable copy can serve it again. That includes asset catalog
metadata, backup and restore coverage and permission to fetch the bytes. A past upload alone does
not prove that a copy is still recoverable.

Specify byte limits for local history, cache and staging, counting database and file usage. Define
the admission policy, free-space reserve, concurrent transfer limits and behavior when protected
data alone exceeds the budget. A cache budget cannot bound offline writes; stop accepting new
writes safely when space runs out and keep saved work. Changing limits must never silently delete
protected data.

Set and justify defaults before calling the implementation ready. The PS-735 workload of 10,000
records and 5 GiB stays unchanged; it is a workload, not a client disk limit. Record steady-state
use and peak space during download, migration, compaction and recovery.
rules.rationale: Consolidated from documentation/requirements/platform/0010-bound-client-storage-and-isolate-sync-failures.md at be10a274555ff00ca839539ee8c90ee5c7428ed2. Requirement status records the source's intent; it is not a claim of implemented, released or verified behavior.

rules.title: 2. Separate synchronization from historical downloads
rules.statement:
Do not download every asset referenced by every receipt before sending unrelated local work or
updating current metadata. Fetch historical content when requested or pinned. Let current content
have a clear not-downloaded state until its local bytes verify. State which records, packages and
assets an environment needs before it is ready offline.

Keep whole-group application and checkpoint atomicity. Relay publication still needs verified
complete bytes; a client with only metadata must not claim to have them. A failed historical fetch
must not stop metadata sync, unrelated uploads or record-only saves. A failed current asset may block
its dependent operation, but not an unrelated group in the same extension owner.

rules.title: 3. Reclaim space without breaking recovery
rules.statement:
Define separate rules for deleting a local cache copy and permanently deleting retained content.
Protect current references, pending work, conflicts, pinned offline files, published revision URLs
and recovery or backup references. In a local-only workbench the local store may be the only
durable copy; remote eviction rules cannot apply until replication is verified.

Add recoverable cleanup for abandoned staging files and unreferenced completed uploads. Account for
an upload that has completed while its commit is still in flight. Tell active from abandoned
transfers across restart. Make cleanup resumable and safe against concurrent writes, and report how
much space it can actually reclaim.

Compact journals and snapshots only with verified coverage that keeps operation identity, outcomes,
revision lineage, deletion markers, dependency ancestry and restore recovery. A TTL alone is not
enough. Captured revisions held by open editors must survive the chosen policy too. Read tokens
include contributing operation IDs, and a save rebuilds its base from journal entries. Define the
retained base or the `expired-revision` contract before removing those entries. Bound revision-token
size and metadata growth. Protecting only queued writes misses an editor's first save.

An identical retry of a known operation returns its retained outcome before needing evicted bytes.
Keep payload fingerprint checks and define how a new operation fetches bytes again.

Define project deletion, retained backups and published-history deletion separately. State whether
each frees local space, removes remote content or affects an existing link. Do not promise that
deleting a record frees all related bytes right away.

rules.title: 4. Amend the sync contracts first
rules.statement:
Compaction and eviction conflict with two existing contracts:

- The earlier synchronization contract kept receipts and immutable versions for replay and
  restore. [Local CRDT storage](../references/architecture/0026-synchronization-contracts.md#durable-local-state)
  now replaces journal replay. PRD 0014 owns the new relay retention rules.
- The synchronization contracts PRD (0007, now deleted) gave retention to later relay work.
  [PRD 0014](book.json) replaces it and owns relay retention and sync failures.

Before any compaction or eviction is turned on, amend both documents or record the change in an ADR.
Link that change from the PR that turns the feature on.

rules.title: 5. Make failures actionable
rules.statement:
Expose local disk usage by category, pending sync, download availability and cleanup results. When
a save cannot proceed, say whether space, bytes, permission, protocol support or a conflict blocks
it. Keep the draft and offer an action that can resolve it. Return these outcomes through public
APIs for both UI and agent callers. The storage PRD adds the
[outcome members](book.json) in 0.44.

rules.title: Gate 2: before eviction, compaction or budget enforcement turns on
rules.statement:
Required changes 1 to 5 are done, the sync contracts are amended (change 4), and this evidence passes:

- Hold current record count and current asset size fixed while historical operations grow. Measure
  journals, snapshots, receipts, indexes, revision tokens, cache and staging separately, and prove
  their limits. Asset eviction alone does not prove bounded metadata use.
- Receive remote metadata when its owner lacks space. Keep saved work and let other owners progress.
- No historical bytes download merely because a current metadata update arrives, except content
  required by policy.
- Exceed the cache budget through repeated history reads. Cache use stays bounded while pending
  work, conflicts, offline pins and remote history are kept.
- Remove or corrupt an old asset and deny its download. Current metadata and an unrelated local save
  in the same owner still sync. Opening that old revision reports its failure.
- Withhold current bytes. Opening the file reports unavailable; unrelated groups still progress. A
  mixed record and asset operation does not falsely publish or report complete local bytes.
- Interrupt upload, record commit and cleanup at each durable boundary. Restart and resume without
  duplicate publication, early deletion or permanent build-up of reclaimable files.
- Read a record, compact its history, then save with the original revision. Cover JSON, text, lists
  and assets. Keep the draft and base guarantees, or return `expired-revision`.
- Commit an asset, replace it, evict its historical bytes, then retry the original identical commit.
  Return its retained outcome; a changed request with the same operation ID still fails.
- Reconnect an offline environment after compaction and relay restore. Keep pending and newer
  accepted work, recover required ancestry and keep conflicts for explicit resolution.
- Exercise local-only workbenches, expired credentials, unsupported peers and migrations that
  exceed the budget. Keep local content and show the next action.
- Record capacity and reconnect results for the unchanged 10,000-record, 5 GiB workload. Do not
  change performance budgets, shrink the workload or skip a platform to pass a check.

Budget enforcement also changes calls that succeed today, so it ships only in a breaking release.

rules.title: Notification status
rules.statement:
The context prefers `id` when both `id` and `dedupeKey` are given; the browser prefers `dedupeKey`.
The context returns `Notification[]`; the bridge returns one notification or a batch wrapper. The
bridge type allows expiry by ID, which the browser rejects. Authors can pass `"expired"` to
`ctx.notify.resolve`, although expiry belongs to the host.

Add these calls in 0.44, with a matching HTTP adapter. Webviews reach them through commands:

```ts
const notification = await ctx.notify.setStatus("review-123", "done"); // Notification | null
const notifications = await ctx.notify.setStatusByKey("review-group", "dismissed"); // Notification[]
```

The single-ID call needs 16 tokens in the prototype; the discarded nested `transition` call needs
43. Do not add a third selector method unless a maintained workflow needs it. Authors may set `done`
and `dismissed`. Missing IDs return `null`; empty groups return `[]`; repeating the same final
status is a no-op. An ID does not grant access to another project.

HTTP has five status routes: `/read`, `/done`, `/dismiss`, `/snooze` and
`/resolve-by-dedupe-key`. `PATCH` also sets `snoozedUntil`. In 0.44 add one status route by ID and
one by key, both taking the status and optional snooze time. `PATCH` stops accepting `snoozedUntil`
in 0.45. The CLI redeclares the client type in its own
[notifications client](../../packages/pstdio/src/adapters/cli/commands/notifications/client.ts);
it must use the SDK `NotificationsClient` type.

The webview capabilities `notification.action`, `.resolve` and `.dismiss` have no callers in
`extensions/` or `.pstdio/extensions/`; only the internal workbench lab fixture uses `.action`. Do
not build `setStatus` parity in the bridge. Keep `notification.show`. Deprecate the three
capabilities, `ctx.notify.resolve`, `ctx.notify.dismiss`, the author `"expired"` status and the old
HTTP routes in 0.44. Remove them in 0.45. Evidence:
[context adapter](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/extensions/command-environment/notifications.ts),
[browser adapter](../../packages/pstdio-dashboard/src/shared/extensions/components/extension-webview-frame.tsx),
[HTTP status routes](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/notifications/endpoints/transition-notification.ts),
[HTTP update route](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/notifications/endpoints/update-notification.ts),
[SDK client](../../packages/sdk/src/client/notifications.ts).

rules.title: Final-status decision for 0.44
rules.statement:
Allow `done` ↔ `dismissed`. A repeated status returns the current notification without a write,
activity entry or sync event. Read and snooze cannot reopen a final item. Host-expired items stay
expired. Key operations lock their project-scoped matching rows and return that snapshot, including
unchanged rows. A notification inserted after selection belongs to the next operation. Legacy
resolve and dismiss adapters share these rules through the same service.

rules.title: Session queries and shapes
rules.statement:
The context `query` already defines the contract: newest first by `created_at`, then `id`;
`includeArchived`; inclusive timestamp bounds; status arrays; and `nextCursor: string | null`. Its
default page size is 50. `list` and `listByWorkspace` were deprecated in 0.43.1 and are removed in
0.44 (PS-805).

Cursor decision for 0.44: keep the immutable creation-time and ID boundary, without a snapshot.
Newer inserts do not shift later pages. Rows archived during paging drop out unless `includeArchived`
is true. Callers keep the same filters across pages; iterators retain them and support cancellation.

The gap is HTTP. [List sessions](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/sessions/endpoints/list-sessions.ts)
is unpaged and takes a single status. In 0.44 add a paged HTTP and SDK query with the same filters
and `{ items, nextCursor }` result, and deprecate the unpaged route. Add SDK `sessions.iterate(filter)`
over `query` so callers read complete results without cursor loops.

Planner's [stack update](../../extensions/pstdio-planner/src/commands/update-stack.ts) refuses
work when another live session uses its workspace; reading only the first page could miss it. It
must filter for live statuses and follow every page. The prototype iterator reads 63 sessions in two
pages; production keeps all query filters and cancellation.

Session and workspace shapes leak storage details.
[`ExtensionSessionSummary`](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/types/sessions.ts)
exposes `workspace_id`, `anchors_json`, `last_selected_model`, `original_session_id` and
`last_request_*`. `sessions.get` has its own inline type with `cwd` and `last_exit`. The
[host adapter](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/extensions/command-environment/sessions.ts)
returns `cwd` from `query`, `list` and `create` too, though their types omit it. The
[workspace adapter](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/extensions/command-environment/workspaces.ts)
casts the database row to `ExtensionWorkspace`, leaking `provider_ref_json`, `provider_error_json`
and `deleted_at`. `CreateExtensionWorkspaceInput` is snake_case.

In 0.44 add camelCase `ExtensionSession` and `ExtensionWorkspace` types and a camelCase create
input. `query`, `get`, `create` and `sessions.iterate` return the new types. In 0.44 the host also
returns the old snake_case fields, marked `@deprecated`, so current callers keep working. Authors
then migrate once in 0.45, when the old fields are removed. The new types carry no anchors; links
come only from `resources`. Use the same types in the SDK client.

The 0.44 workspace type keeps its existing optional properties and adds optional camelCase
properties so older callers can still construct sparse workspace values. Host readers always fill
the camelCase fields. Deprecated snake_case fields, including `anchors_json`, remain only for
the compatibility window. The new session type has no anchor field; readers intersect it with
the deprecated summary during that window. Provider references, errors and deletion metadata
are never part of the command workspace projection.

Use the same page rules for other large histories, such as automation runs. The 0.44 list decision is below.

No resource or dynamic catalog list in this PRD or PRD 0012 F qualifies for an unpaged exception:
the current agent, model, provider and board registries have no enforced finite size bound.
Projects, workspaces, skills, sessions and saved views must page. Agent, model, provider and board
catalogs also page. The canonical limit is 50 by default and at most 200; resource links keep their
existing maximum of 100. No existing data is truncated to meet these limits.

Unpaged routes and methods remain deprecated compatibility readers through 0.44, not bounded
catalog exceptions. Finite vocabularies embedded in records, such as enum choices, are not resource
collection endpoints. File storage and filesystem listing capacity remain owned by PRDs 0009 and
0010; this decision does not invent a bound for them. See the
[client conventions](../references/extensions/0023-client-conventions.md) for cursor ordering,
null rules, per-read behavior and canonical routes.

rules.title: Resource links
rules.statement:
Use `ctx.resources.addAnchors`, `removeAnchors` and `listAnchors` for existing resources:

```ts
await ctx.resources.addAnchors({ type: "session", id: sessionId }, [{ type: "ticket", id: ticketId }]);
```

An owner is needed only when it is ambiguous. `ResourceRef.extensionId` is optional.
[`canonicalResource`](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/extensions/command-environment/resource-link-policy.ts)
fills it: host kinds (`project`, `workspace`, `session`) get `pstdio`, then a kind owned by the
calling extension, then the only owner of that kind. It throws when none of these rules applies.

Host sources must exist in the current project. Generic and legacy additions and removals lock
that source row, commit the entire batch in one transaction, and update its timestamp only when
links change. A missing, deleted or foreign host source is refused before any edge is written.
The project, workspace and session tables own these checks; no extra link status is stored.
Extension-owned references remain under their resource kind's validation policy because their
records and timestamps belong to the extension. A declared kind may describe a virtual resource.

Dedicated columns own source identity, target identity and role. Equivalent legacy details that
omit those fields are the same link. Repeating either API does not update a timestamp or emit a
changed-link event. Label, metadata and role changes still count as changes. Validation hooks,
owner inference, removal checks and changed-link events remain shared.

`sessions.addAnchors`/`removeAnchors` and `workspaces.addAnchors`/`removeAnchors` are marked
`@deprecated` in 0.44 and removed in 0.45. Keep anchors passed during resource creation, where the
host saves creation and linkage together. Evidence:
[generic adapter](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/extensions/command-environment/resource-links.ts),
[legacy transaction](../../packages/pstdio-db/src/services/legacy-resource-links.ts).

rules.title: Command results, errors and streams
rules.statement:
The kernel has a discriminated `CommandOutcome`. The HTTP outcome schema accepts `ok` and `status`
separately, including contradictory pairs. The typed webview unwraps a failure into a plain `Error`
and loses its code, data and diagnostics. HTTP and webview stream clients end in different shapes.

The host loses rejections too.
[`workbench-extension-command.ts`](../../packages/pstdio-workbench/src/extensions/host/workbench-extension-command.ts)
calls `unwrapCommandValue`, so webviews get a plain `Error`. In the dashboard's
[webview command router](../../packages/pstdio-dashboard/src/shared/extensions/components/extension-webview-command.ts),
an ID without `.command.` runs as a workbench command and returns a raw value. PS-805 fixes the
host path. The shared outcome contract below covers that path too.

In 0.44 add a shared validated outcome contract and adapters. Keep success values, rejection codes
and data, causes, diagnostics and notices; keep transport metadata outside. A throwing helper is
optional and must carry the complete outcome. Recommend explicit outcomes for recoverable rejections.

Add a command stream with iterable chunks, a final outcome promise and cancellation. Specify early
return, cancellation before start, disconnect and rejected completion. Keep backpressure and bounds.
A disconnected client must not re-run a command that has external effects.

The 0.44 stream contract is `CommandStream<TChunk, TResult>` in `/extensions`. Webviews use
`client.streams.<command>()`; HTTP clients use `client.extensions.streamCommand(projectId,
commandId, input?, options?)`. Each stream has one chunk consumer. Every terminal path closes the
chunks and resolves `outcome`, including rejection and transport failure. `getCommandValue` throws
`CommandOutcomeError` with the complete failed outcome when the caller needs a value.

Cancellation before start opens no subscription. `cancel()`, an aborted signal and early iterator
return stop the remote command, clear unread chunks and resolve a cancelled outcome. Local cleanup
never waits for a remote acknowledgement. Disconnect closes the subscription with a structured error
outcome and its original cause; it never reconnects that command. Existing byte bounds and host
backpressure stay in place. Deprecated webview `.result` still returns the value or rejects, and the
old HTTP event iterator remains callable through 0.44.

`validatedCommandOutcomeSchema` validates the kernel union and `commandExecutionResultSchema`
wraps it with transport metadata. The old object schemas stay callable, including their Zod object
methods, until removal. Existing SDK `execute` returns the canonical result intersected with the old
optional fields during 0.44, preserving source compatibility for unguarded legacy field access.

A ticket save rejected with `stale_revision` keeps its draft and conflict details in a webview or
an external client. Deprecate the old schemas and adapters in 0.44; remove them in 0.45.
Evidence: [kernel outcomes](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/types/commands.ts),
[HTTP schema](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extensions/execute.ts),
[unwrap helper](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/command-outcome.ts),
[webview streams](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/webview-streams.ts),
[HTTP streams](../../packages/sdk/src/client/extension-stream.ts).

rules.title: Settings and preferences
rules.statement:
Keep settings and preferences separate. Settings belong to an installed extension or a project
instance. Preferences have user, project, workspace and session scopes with fallbacks.

Add the missing typed webview `settings.delete` wrapper in 0.44; the bridge capability exists.
Deleting a project override restores the declared fallback instead of storing `null`.

Keep caller-owned preference names, including dynamic names, and the supported core preferences.
Deprecate access to another extension's preference names in 0.44 and remove it in 0.45. Evidence:
[typed settings client](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/webview-client.ts),
[preference owner](../../packages/pstdio-workbench/src/extensions/bridge/webview-preferences-capability.ts).

rules.title: Saved views and renderer options
rules.statement:
Use `ViewFilterGroup`, ordered `ViewSort[]` and an explicit default-view ID across saved views,
board and table queries, UI controls, CLI and HTTP. The flat `filters`, single-sort `ordering`,
`defaultFilters`, `isDefault` and `onReorder` were deprecated in 0.43.1. In 0.44 the host stops
sending `filters` and `ordering` and the types drop them (PS-805). Keep compound filters, relative
dates, manual order, built-in views, custom titles and default selection when converting saved views.

Status contributions were also deprecated in 0.43.1 and are removed in 0.44. Extensions return enum
options and `boardColumnConfigs` from their queries. Use `onMove` to save a complete drag. Keep
`onAttributeChange` for inline edits. Do not delete `StatusBarItemContribution`; it is a different
feature. Evidence: [renderer contract](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/types/kanban-renderer.ts),
[saved views](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/board-views.ts),
[public UI view type](../../packages/ui/src/components/collection-view/collection-view-types.ts).

rules.title: Workspace lifecycle, navigation and file links
rules.statement:
Use `workspaces.delete`, the provider `delete` hook and `capabilities.delete`. The archive method,
hook, capability and event were deprecated in 0.43.1 and are removed in 0.44 (PS-805).

The HTTP [workspace contract](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/workspaces.ts) also
used `capabilities.archive`. That field was already deprecated in stable 0.43.1, so PS-805 removes
it in 0.44 along with the extension capability. Do not restore it for a second deprecation window.

The remaining HTTP `provider_operation_kind: "archive"` value is deprecated in 0.44. Use
`"delete"` for new operations. Keep returning the original value for historical operations until
0.45; deprecating this value does not deprecate the supported `create`, `cancel` and `delete`
values or rewrite stored history. Stored rows may still keep `archive` in
[`provider_capabilities_json`](../../packages/pstdio-db/src/db/schemas/workspaces.ts), plus
`archiving` and `archived` provider states. In 0.45 remove the legacy operation value and convert
stored rows. Generate any schema change with `db:generate`; never hand-write schema SQL.

PS-805 now emits `workspace.deleted` through the
[kernel slots](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/kernel-slots.ts).
Consumers that replace `archived` with `deleted` build on that prerequisite.

Share `NavigationTarget` and owner-aware file links across command results, browser navigation,
message renderers and CLI opening. Keep page params, resource identity, workspace, source position
and preview or pin intent. Calls without a UI navigation scope still drop navigation requests. A
bare path must not pick another machine or the default workspace. The chat `onOpenFile` props were
deprecated in 0.43.1 for `linkHandler` and are removed in 0.44.
Evidence: [workspace API](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/types/workspaces.ts),
[navigation targets](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/types/navigation-target.ts),
[resource path requirements](book.json).

rules.title: SDK helper exports and old hook contexts
rules.statement:
The [hooks entry point](../../packages/sdk/src/hooks/index.ts) exports filesystem-hook context
types, the `BaseHookContext.payload` mirror and a singular `client.session.followup` facade. No
extension imports `@pstdio/sdk/hooks`. These exports and compatibility members are deprecated
in 0.44 and removed in 0.45. Typed extension hooks use their declared context fields; external SDK
clients use the plural `client.sessions.followUp(sessionId, input)` method. Keep
lifecycle payloads that typed host slots still need.

Deprecate [`requireRepoFiles`](../../packages/sdk/src/data/draft-layout.ts) in 0.44 and remove
it in 0.45 after the replacement ships. Planner and Reports pass `ctx.projectFiles` into it; they
move to the named file handle from PRD 0009 in separate extension PRs using its published SDK.
Keep the pure frontmatter, draft-layout, name-resolution and prompt-rendering helpers.

rules.title: A. One webview host capability factory
rules.statement:
The workbench, dashboard and testbench use one
`createExtensionWebviewHostCapabilities(adapters)`.
It owns every capability name, parameter checks, result wrappers, and frame stream lifetime.
Hosts supply typed service adapters. They cannot replace capability handlers.

Workbench adapters bind navigation, placement, preferences and native commands. The extension
command adapter adds project, slot and resource ownership. Dashboard adapters bind API services
for settings, streams, notifications, files and artifacts. The testbench supplies its command
service, in-memory files and scripted terminal through the same workbench registration path.

Every host exposes the same capability names. A missing service produces
`WebviewHostCapabilityError` with `code: "unsupported"` and `data.capability`. Invalid input
produces `code: "invalid_params"` before invoking a service. Command execution preserves the
complete outcome, including rejections. Stream cancellation, disconnect behavior, and the
existing 16-stream and 8 MiB unread-data limits have one owner in the factory.

[Host adapter reference](../references/workbench/0005-webview-hosts.md).

Change level: none for extensions. This is internal to the hosts. Theme B adds guest error
transport and typed client methods separately.

rules.title: B. Typed webview client
rules.statement:
[`WebviewClient`](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/webview-client.ts) wraps only `artifacts`,
`commands`, `streams`, `events` and `settings`. Extensions call the rest through raw `host.call`:
`navigation.open` 7 times, `notification.show` 3, `preferences.get`/`set` 2 and `placement.close` 1.

Add `client.navigation.open(target)`, `client.placement.close()`, `client.notify.toast(notice)` and
`client.preferences.get`/`set`. Fold the render-context page and files clients in
[`define-extension-view.ts`](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/define-extension-view.ts) into
the one `WebviewClient`.

Host props are typed `unknown`. The dashboard sends eight props, the workbench two and the testbench
five. Add `WebviewHostProps` to the contracts with `projectId`, `themePreference`, `locale`,
`resource`, `pageLocation`, `pageParams` and `translations`. Deprecate `lastCommand`; extension-lab
uses it to trigger refreshes. The replacement is `client.events.subscribe`.

Other shape fixes:

- Bridge errors reach the guest as `new Error(message)`; gate denial codes go only to diagnostics
  ([capability gate](../../packages/pstdio-extensions/src/bridge/contract/capabilities.ts)).
  Capability errors carry `{ code, message, data? }`.
- `WebviewNotificationShowParams` is `{ level, title, message? }`, while `CommandNotice` is
  `{ type, title?, message }`. `notification.show` accepts `CommandNotice`; deprecate the old shape.
- `extension.settings.set` returns nothing; `preferences.set` returns the saved value. Make
  `settings.set` return the saved value too.
- [`useCommandQuery`](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/react/index.ts) has no refresh option.
  Seven extensions, one of them a skill example, write their own subscribe-and-refetch loop. Add
  `refreshOn: { client, events }`.

Deprecate APIs with no extension callers: the `terminal.session` capability and
[`createTerminalSessionBridge`](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/terminal-session-bridge.ts),
the render-context page client, and `files.list`/`files.delete` (only the internal workbench lab
fixture calls them). No extension declares a versioned capability such as `"clipboard.write@1"`;
only host tests use the form. Deprecate it.

Change level: additive in 0.44. Removing the old shapes and refusing versioned declarations is
breaking in 0.45.

rules.title: C. Context shape
rules.statement:
[`CommandContext.invocation`](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/types/context.ts)
repeats the top-level `source`, `attachment` and `slot`; only its `metadata` is new. No extension
reads it. Move `metadata` to the top level and deprecate `invocation`.

The base context declares `source`, but only command contexts set it. Declare `source` on
`CommandContext` and deprecate it on the base. Deprecate `project`; no extension reads it.

Only `CommandContext` has `signal`. Workspace providers get theirs from
`WorkspaceProviderCreateInput.signal` (`extension.ts`). Add `signal` to `ExtensionContextBase` and
deprecate the input field.

`ctx.notify.toast` is a silent no-op outside commands. Only the command runner
([environment](../../packages/pstdio-extensions/src/runtime/runner/environment.ts)) collects
notices. Add `CommandContext.notices.add(notice)` and deprecate `toast`.

`SetupContext` and `MigrationContext` are unused aliases. No extension reads `EventContext.eventId`
or `deliveryId`. Deprecate all four. `skills` is optional, but the production host always sets it.
Make it required; the testbench must then provide it.

rules.title: D. Services with no callers
rules.statement:
No extension calls these context services. Packages outside the host wiring do not call them either:

| Service | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.terminal` | `context.ts` |
| `ctx.net.findFreePort` | `context.ts` |
| `ctx.connections.stream` | `connections.ts` |
| `ctx.activity.record` | `context.ts` |
| `ctx.automation.get`, `cancel` | `automation.ts` |
| `getQueuedFollowUps`, `updateQueuedFollowUp`, `combineQueuedFollowUps`, `steerQueuedFollowUp` | `sessions.ts` |
| `ctx.views.reorder` | `saved-views.ts` |

The CLI uses HTTP client methods with the queued-input names; those stay. 0011 used to keep
`terminal`, `net`, `activity` and queued input. Deprecate them in 0.44 unless a supported caller
appears before the contracts freeze. `ctx.resources.removeAnchors` also has no callers, but it
replaces the session and workspace wrappers that 0011 deprecates, so it stays.

rules.title: E. Naming and lookups
rules.statement:
`ctx.views.remove` (`saved-views.ts`) returns `{ deleted }`; every other API deletes with `delete`.
Add `views.delete` with the same result and deprecate `remove`. It has one Planner caller.

Lookups by ID return `null` when the record is missing, as `workspaces.get` and `sessions.get` do.
`automation.get` returns `undefined`; D deprecates it, so leave it. New lookups follow the rule.

`workspaces.get(id)` and `workspaces.getByShorthand(shorthand)` both return a workspace. Make
`get` accept either, with an ID match first, and deprecate `getByShorthand`. Reports and Planner
call it.

If a supported caller keeps the queued-input methods (see D), give them one object input, like
`create` and `followup`, instead of `(sessionId, queuePosition, input)`.

`automation.enqueue` accepts a `CommandRef`, but
[`AutomationRun.commandId`](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/automation.ts) is a string
the host builds as `<extension>.command.<id>`. Add `command: CommandRef` and deprecate `commandId`.

`process.run` and `process.runOrThrow` both exist. Document that `run` is for callers that inspect
the exit code and `runOrThrow` for callers that treat a non-zero exit as an error.

Change level: additive in 0.44, breaking in 0.45. The process note is documentation only.

rules.title: F. Resource and client conventions
rules.statement:
The SDK client and HTTP contracts mix conventions:

- Casing: [activity](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/activity.ts), sessions, workspaces,
  [skills](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/skills.ts) and filesystem inputs use
  snake_case. Notifications, automation and command execution use camelCase.
- Lists: notifications, resource links and session pages return `{ items, nextCursor }` with three
  different null rules. Activity returns `{ events, next_cursor }`. Projects, workspaces, skills,
  sessions and saved views return unpaged arrays.
- Project scope: `workspaces.list(projectId)` takes it first, `notifications.create({ projectId })`
  and `workspaces.create({ project_id })` take it in the input.
- The project query parameter is `project_id` for workspaces and sessions, `projectId` for auth
  tokens and `project` for agent info.

Use camelCase JSON, `{ items, nextCursor: string | null }` for paged lists, `projectId` as the first
SDK argument and `projectId` as the query parameter. 0011 defines the session and workspace types.
Page every named dynamic catalog, following 0011's final decision without a small-catalog exemption.

Change level: the SDK client is not in the extension API report today (see N). It follows the same
deprecate-then-remove rule. Granite calls `createClient` and `client.projects` from outside this
repository, so `/client` changes break scripts.

rules.title: G. Actions and when conditions
rules.statement:
`KanbanRendererRowAction`, `DataTableRendererRowAction` and `DataTableRendererSelectionAction`
(`kanban-renderer.ts`, `data-table-renderer.ts`) have the same fields. The wire format already
uses one schema. Add `CollectionAction { id, label, icon?, destructive?, command }` and keep the
three names as deprecated aliases.

`ActivityItemContribution` (`contributions.ts`) uses `command` and `params`, while navigation
items, tab menu rows and keybindings use `action: NavigationTarget`. Use `action` with `title` as
the label, and deprecate `command` and `params`.

Menus, keybindings and navigation items take a `WhenExpression` object. `ViewToolbarAction.when`
(`view-toolbar-action.ts`) and `TreeAction.when` (`tree-renderer.ts`) take a string. Accept
`WhenExpression` in both and deprecate the string form.

rules.title: H. Form schemas
rules.statement:
Four schema dialects describe form fields: `ParamDescriptor` (`params.ts`), `ControlParam`
(`control-declarations.ts`), `ExtensionSettingProperty` (`contributions.ts`) and
`PageParamDefinition` (`pages.ts`). They spell labels, defaults and types differently.

`KanbanRendererCreateRowContribution` declares its own `params` next to the command it calls.
Planner shows the cost. Its [form](../../extensions/pstdio-planner/src/ticket-create-form.ts)
makes `content` required markdown and adds `files`. The
[command](../../extensions/pstdio-planner/src/commands/create-ticket.ts) takes optional long text
and has no `files` parameter. The dialog strips the files and attaches them with a second command.
The command's own `attachments` parameter is never filled.

`createRow` reuses the command's params, with `fields?: string[]` to choose which to show. The host
owns the dialog's cancel, error and file-removal labels; deprecate `createRow.labels` and
`createRow.params`. New form APIs use `ParamDescriptor`.

rules.title: J. Slots
rules.statement:
The [metadata adapter](../../packages/pstdio-workbench/src/extensions/host/workbench-extension-metadata-adapter.ts)
places settings panels by checking whether the slot ID contains `"global"`, and status bar items by
checking whether it ends with `"leading"`. No built-in settings slot ID contains `"global"`. Add
`SettingsPanelContribution.target: "global" | "project"` and `StatusBarItemContribution.side:
"leading" | "trailing"`, and stop reading placement from slot IDs.

ID matching already fails once. The dashboard
[wrapper](../../packages/pstdio-dashboard/src/shared/extensions/extension-webview-capabilities.ts)
gives settings panels file capabilities only for slot `project.settingsPanels`. Planner's panel uses
`project.settings`, so it never matches. That bug belongs in PS-805.

`UiSlotKind` (`slots.ts`) has six values; the host checks only `menu`. `panel` and `settings` come
only from kernel slots with no users: `projectSlots.sidenav`, `projectSlots.settingsPanels`,
`workspaceSlots.sidenav` and `sessionSlots`. Deprecate those slots and the two kinds.

rules.title: K. Events
rules.statement:
[Event names](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extension-kernel/kernel-slots.ts) mix
styles: `session.awaitingInput` is camelCase, `view.board-views.changed` is kebab-case, and
`workspace.provision` is a noun. Use `noun.past-tense` names in kebab-case. Keep old names as
deprecated aliases.

`workspace.provision` is awaited and gates readiness
([coordinator](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/workspaces/provision-coordinator.ts)). It
is a hook, not an event. Add a provider hook and deprecate the event.

Payloads disagree. Workspace events have no `projectId`; the others do. Session payloads repeat
`workspaceId`, `branch` and `workspaceDir` next to `workspace`, and
[session hooks](../../packages/pstdio-api/src/features/hooks/session-hooks.ts) can make
`workspaceDir` and `workspace.root_path` disagree. `session.started` and `session.completed` add
`anchors` again and merge workspace anchors without removing duplicates. Use a fixed envelope
`{ projectId, workspace? }` with a typed body. Drop `anchors`; links come from `resources`.

Some events have no producer: `project.opened` (3 Planner consumers), `workspace.created`,
`workspace.deleted`, `git.committed`, `git.rebased`, `git.conflicted` and
`view.repositories.changed`. PS-805 emits the used ones. Deprecate the rest unless a producer ships.

rules.title: M. Author repetition
rules.statement:
`PageContribution` (`pages.ts`) requires `title` and `slots`. Font Editor writes "Icon Set editor"
on its view, page and navigation item, and ten extension files declare `slots: []`. Default a page
title and icon to its main view's, and a navigation item's label and icon to its page's. Make
`slots` optional.

The public `PackageManifest` (`extension.ts`) lacks `pstdio.projectFiles.tracked`, which the
[runtime manifest](../../packages/pstdio-extensions/src/runtime/package-manifest.ts) validates.
Keep one type.

Resource kinds are `resourceKind: ResourceKindRef`, `resourceKind?: string`,
`resourceType: ResourceKindRef[]`, `resourceType: string` or `kinds`. Accept `ResourceKindRef`
everywhere under the name `resourceKind`.

Do not merge IDs that are separate on purpose, such as a widget `id` and its `rendererId`.

rules.title: N. SDK public surface
rules.statement:
The SDK exports `/extensions`, `/extensions/react`, `/testing`, `/data`, `/prompts`, `/hooks`,
`/client`, `/api` and `/resources`. No extension imports `/client`, `/api`, `/resources` or
`/hooks`. In-repo hosts import `/api` in about 155 files, including the published
`@pstdio/workbench` and `@pstdio/ui`. Granite imports `/client`. In 0.44, list the public subpaths
in 0014 and decide, per subpath, between "public, in the API report" and "host-only, deprecated".

[`/extensions`](../../packages/sdk/src/extensions/index.ts) exports host-only values with no
extension callers: `WEBVIEW_*` constants, `ALWAYS_AVAILABLE_WEBVIEW_CAPABILITIES`,
`EXTENSION_EVENTS_SCOPE`, `resolveEventReferenceId`, `qualifyNavigationTarget`, page-param helpers,
`parseWorkbenchPageUrl`, `serializeWorkbenchPageUrl` and `resolveDataTable*`. `mergeOrderedHistory`
and `artifactMountId` are used only inside their packages. `host.dispatchKeyboardEvent` is in the
public capability union, although no extension may call it. Hosts import these from
`pstdio-api-contracts` directly; deprecate the SDK exports.

The dashboard builds about 75 raw `/v1` paths in 34 files through the untyped request helper in
[`api.ts`](../../packages/pstdio-dashboard/src/lib/api.ts), and calls `createClient` twice. Route
it through the typed client, then delete client methods that still have no callers.

Some names have two meanings or two homes. `TerminalSessionAdapter` is one type in
[`/api`](../../packages/pstdio-api-contracts/src/extensions.terminal.ts) and a different one in
`/extensions`. B removes the second; if it stays, rename it `ExtensionTerminalSession`.
`AssetReference` and `AssetTransfer` come from `/client` and `/extensions`. Notification types
come from `/api` and `/extensions`. Give each type one export path.

2. Classify each as documentation error, implementation gap, proposed work, missing acceptance evidence, or environment blocker. Do not simply rewrite the PRD to bless destructive behavior.
5. Implement the chosen contract at its owning layer; align the PRD, CLI help, general skill, and authoring references. Validate actual agent-directory installation for first install, reinstall, edited existing content, and packaged assets. Reuse the installer tests and add meaningful cases for the chosen contract.

rules.title: W8: Final fresh-agent and release gate
rules.statement:
Use new agents with no prior conversation, audit results, application source checkout, or other agent's artifacts. Give each an independent disposable author environment **and app host**, actual packaged skills, public documentation access, and the same written task. Record exact prompts, package/host/API versions, OS, commands, errors, interventions, source artifacts, and observed outcomes. Keep credentials out of evidence.

Run these trials after packaging the final guidance:

1. **Create an extension:** a Reading List-style tool with title/URL, add/edit, read state, All/Unread filters, delete, native UI, CLI parity, reload persistence, live refresh, and two-project separation.
2. **Edit an existing extension:** add a field/action to a supplied working extension, preserve existing data, and verify the changed UI and CLI. Confirm the agent edits canonical source rather than an installed copy.
3. **Use first-party skills:** create/refine/implement dependent Planner work, write a Report, and publish an Artifact. Verify the right docs are reached, dependencies are modeled correctly, output paths are owned correctly, and resource links/opening behave as documented.
4. **Diagnose version mismatch:** first pass all workflows with aligned stable versions. Then deliberately mismatch tooling and host in a separate trial; require correct diagnosis and recovery without unsupported compatibility claims.

Pass criteria: Required operations work through public interfaces; data persists and remains project-scoped; exports contain every referenced asset; links resolve; no author needs application internals or undisclosed manual repair. Record SDK-type lookup separately from genuine dead ends. Repeat failed trials after the responsible fix with another fresh context. Do not claim a measured improvement from one agent per condition.

Before closing, all applicable CI checks must pass on each implementation PR's latest commit. Add required changesets for changed packages/extensions, release through the normal workflow, deploy the public docs, and repeat the released-package/public-site smoke journey. Keep “merged,” “released,” and “verified after release” separate. Coordinate release authority under the normal repository process.

rules.title: Outcome and boundary
rules.statement:
A person opens a cloud project on a new device, chooses a new folder, and gets every
included project-folder file that reached Cloud. Saved edits, new files and local Git data
come back without a Git hosting service. No commit or push is required.

This fits the [mission](book.json): storage, encryption and recovery belong
in core because every tool needs them. The Cloud extension owns progress and recovery
UI through public APIs. Extensions keep owning their records and declared files.

Automatic upload and download keep a recoverable copy on the user's devices. This
first outcome does not continuously apply remote source edits to an active folder.
Editor buffers must be saved to disk. Terminal and process execution do not move to
another device; their saved files do. Existing session history keeps its device owner.

rules.title: Folder coverage and `.pstignore`
rules.statement:
The project folder is the inclusion boundary. Include everything except paths matched
by the root `.pstignore`. `.gitignore`, Git tracked/untracked state, global Git rules
and extension cache declarations do not filter the folder capture. The same rule works
without Git installed and for non-Git projects.

When a new folder is first enrolled without an inherited capture policy, create a
missing `.pstignore` with this starter rule. Do not overwrite an existing file or
recreate a deleted one:

```text
node_modules/
```

This skips dependency directories at any depth. Users can remove that rule or add
their own, such as `.cache/` or `dist/`. There are no other built-in path exclusions.
An empty or deliberately deleted `.pstignore` means all project-folder files are
included. `.env` and `.env.*` are not in the starter rules and remain included even
when `.gitignore` excludes them.

Restoring a capture inherits its applied policy, including an empty file or deliberate
absence. Starting capture on that new device must not seed a starter policy over the
restored choice. Record absence in the manifest, so round-trip recovery preserves it
without a separate local preference flag.

Use one UTF-8 `.pstignore` at the project root. Nested `.pstignore` files are ordinary
files, not additional policies. Use familiar ignore-file patterns: `#` comments,
`*`, `?` and `**` globs, `/` for root-relative patterns, a trailing `/` for directories,
and `!` for re-inclusion. A pattern without a slash matches a name at any depth.
The last matching rule wins. An excluded parent must be re-included before any child
can be re-included. Escaped leading `#` and `!` match literal names.

Always include the root `.pstignore` itself, including under broad patterns such as
`*`. Store its exact contents and applied rules with each encrypted manifest. Read
the policy as a regular file without following links. An unreadable, invalid or
changing policy blocks a new capture; never silently fall back to including files.
Re-scan when it changes, and verify it is unchanged before publishing the manifest.

| Data inside the project folder | Required treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Saved source, binaries, new files, dotfiles, empty directories and executable bits | Include unless matched by `.pstignore`. No commit or push is needed. |
| `.git`, nested repositories and submodule files | Include unless matched by `.pstignore`, including objects, index, refs, reflogs, config and hooks. No separate Git opt-in. |
| `.env`, key files and other credential-bearing files | Include unless explicitly matched by `.pstignore`, encrypted on the client before transfer. No secret-pattern exclusions. |
| `node_modules`, build output, caches and Git-ignored files | Apply `.pstignore` only. The starter file excludes `node_modules/`; build output and caches remain included until users add rules. Size or transfer failures are not exclusions. |
| `.pstdio/config.json`, `.pstdio/extensions` and `.pstdio/extension-storage` content | Include unless matched by `.pstignore`, including local extension code, caches, drafts, reports and nested workspace files. Preserve publisher paths. |
| Files already represented by extension records or declared mounts | Apply `.pstignore` to their on-disk capture. This does not change the separate shared-record or declared-file sync owner. The scanner is read-only. |
| Root `.pstignore` | Always retain the exact applied policy with the capture. |
| Included symlinks | Retain the link and its exact target text without following it. An external target does not become part of the project folder. |
| Unreadable, changing or unsupported included entries | Report the entry as pending or blocked. Do not skip it and mark the included copy complete. |

List excluded paths or directory roots with the matching rule, separately from errors
and pending entries. Do not read or upload excluded file contents. Excluding a directory
does not require traversing its contents. A complete capture means all included data
under the displayed policy, not a full copy of excluded paths.

Changing a rule changes coverage in the next manifest. Newly excluded paths leave the
current capture after it completes; they are not filesystem deletions and do not
delete local files. Re-included paths must finish uploading before the new capture is
complete. Previous captures and grace-period blobs can still contain previously
included bytes; changing `.pstignore` is not an immediate purge of stored history.

For included entries, preserve supported metadata, including permissions and link information. If the
source or destination cannot retain an entry or its required metadata, explain the
limitation and keep the operation incomplete. A socket or device entry is not a
running process that can be copied; detecting one must produce an explicit unsupported
entry rather than a successful partial backup.

Files outside the project folder are outside this requirement. Workspace records
still recover through private project data, but a workspace path outside the folder
does not imply its files are retained. Show that boundary. Do not search the whole
machine or follow links to copy unrelated folders. Referenced Git administration
needed to restore an included worktree is handled explicitly below.

rules.title: Ownership and encryption
rules.statement:
A complete folder can contain private workspaces, credentials and historical private
files inside `.git`. Keep the entire per-source folder capture in the source user's
private project data, encrypted with that user's private-project-data key (R13).
Only that user's devices can read it. Membership in a shared project does not grant
access to another member's raw folder capture. Do not split a Git object graph by
current pathname or copy private subtrees into a shared manifest.

Existing shared records and declared shared files keep their current public APIs,
owners and project-key encryption. File recovery is a captured filesystem state,
not another live writer of extension records. Restore must not race the existing
file projection or run extension migrations on half-restored files.

Relay document and blob IDs are opaque. Filenames, paths, content hashes, Git refs,
configuration and file bytes stay encrypted. The relay stores and routes ciphertext;
it does not inspect folders. Logs and transport errors contain no readable paths or
content. This extends the current encryption and access rules, not the trust of
other project members.

Folder captures follow R15 and R37 for device removal: revoke future service access
and rotate keys for future data. A removed device can still decrypt older ciphertext
with keys it already received and keep its downloaded files. Removal cannot erase
those copies or retroactively revoke their encryption keys. Remaining devices keep
old keys for historical recovery; this feature adds no remote-wipe promise.

rules.title: Git and device-specific files
rules.statement:
Capture `.git` under the same `.pstignore` policy. When included, retain its files,
including local-only objects, staged data, reflogs, hooks and configuration. Excluding
Git administration or required objects must disable the functional Git recovery claim;
do not claim a partial object graph is a complete repository. Do not substitute a clone,
rewrite history, filter historical secrets or require a second consent step. The
private audience above covers both current files and historical objects. `.pstignore`
filters filesystem paths, not content embedded inside Git objects. An excluded working
file can still exist in retained Git history; do not rewrite or silently filter commits.

A worktree or submodule can use a `.git` file that points to administration outside
the folder. When Git administration is included, automatically capture the referenced administration and required object
stores as private Git recovery dependencies, with cycle detection and source identity.
Inventory these dependencies separately from folder entries. If they are unavailable,
the folder bytes can still be retained, but functional Git recovery stays incomplete.
This exception does not mean following arbitrary filesystem symlinks.

External targets must belong to the owning repository's canonical administration or
object-store roots already trusted through local project/workspace registration.
Derive that boundary from the existing local registration, not a new allow-list from
project files. Validate the worktree/submodule relationship and every resolved path
against those roots before reading. A `.git`, `commondir` or `alternates` pointer by
itself grants no permission to read another directory. Reject unregistered roots,
unrelated folders and links that escape the allowed roots; report Git recovery as
incomplete. Recheck the boundary during reads so path replacement cannot widen it.
Inspect metadata without running repository hooks, filters or configuration commands.

Restoration retains captured original bytes. Where worktree pointers or device bindings
need a new path, retain the original in the recovery store and record the local mapping
and changed materialized paths in the restore result. Rebuild Git administration links
inside the restored recovery layout; never leave a dependency on the source device.
Do not silently discard config or hooks. Recovery itself must not execute retained
hooks, scripts, provisioning, automations or local extension code. Installation,
activation and execution follow the normal trust and setup flow after recovery.

rules.title: Capture and encrypted storage
rules.statement:
Use one core recovery owner for each source device's project folder. Each publishes
one current complete manifest through an encrypted private document. List source
identity, capture interval, applied `.pstignore`, exclusions, relative paths, entry
types, metadata, content digests, chunk references and Git recovery dependencies. An encrypted private catalog discovers
these sources. Existing workspace/device identities provide ownership; no second
stored project status is needed.

Keep separate source copies when devices edit independently. A restored device
publishes its own source entry. Never let one device's upload overwrite another's
unsent work through an arbitrary latest-device or wall-clock rule.

Read every included entry. Watch filesystem changes, including `.pstignore` edits and writes by external tools, to
schedule capture. Reconcile with a full scan on startup, reconnect, watcher overflow
and an explicit “Back up now” action. Persist pending work across restarts. Watch
notifications are hints, not proof that all entries were scanned.

Read changing files and Git state again before completing capture. A scan error is
never interpreted as a deletion. A successful complete scan represents a deletion
by absence from the new manifest. A rename is a removed path and an added path that
can reuse content. Unreadable or continuously changing entries keep current work
pending while the previous complete capture remains restorable.

Ordinary scans are not one atomic instant across unrelated external writes. Show
the capture interval. Preserve platform atomic multi-file save boundaries (R4).
Include database files unless excluded by `.pstignore`, but do not promise an application-consistent image
of a running external database. Its changing or unverified files remain pending.

Split large files into independently encrypted bounded chunks and use resumable blob
storage. Reuse unchanged chunks only within the same encryption space. Do not expose
plaintext hashes or deduplicate across accounts on the relay. Persist manifests and
ciphertext references durably; publish a completed cloud manifest only after all
referenced blobs are acknowledged (R21). Interrupted transfers resume with the same
references. Failure never replaces the previous completed capture with a partial one.

Keep the recovery service's own cache, manifests and staging outside captured roots.
If the configured runtime home overlaps the project folder, relocate that service's
working storage outside it before capture or report a setup error. Do not silently
exclude a project subtree or recursively back up the capture's own output.

R20/R21's grace period protects referenced blobs during replacement. Relay retention
is latest state plus the grace copy, not a permanent history of captures. Define
participation of these owners in R53's client history during implementation; do not
claim the existing snapshot code already covers folder captures.

rules.title: Download and restore
rules.statement:
Each user's devices automatically download their completed source captures and bytes
into a local recovery store, even before choosing a project folder. This preserves
offline recovery under R1. It does not project another device's edits or deletions
into an active folder. List source devices and capture intervals so a person can
choose a recoverable copy without depending on the source device being online.

Restore into a new, absent destination. Refuse an existing destination without writes,
even when empty. Offer a new sibling folder or the existing attach workflow. Attaching
local work is not restoration. When the project already has a folder, restore another
source as a separate workspace and keep the current folder attached.

Validate the entire manifest and destination capabilities before publication. Check
path traversal, case collisions, reserved names, permissions and unsupported entry
types. Preserve symlink target text, but never follow restored links for writes.
Use a sibling staging directory on the same filesystem, an operation journal and
resumable verified downloads. Publish with a platform-supported no-replace operation;
a check followed by an ordinary replacing rename is insufficient. Concurrent creation
of the destination must preserve that work and leave restoration incomplete.

Attach only after all entries and Git dependencies are verified and publication is
complete. Reconcile local device bindings without erasing the retained original files.
Pause live file projection and extension setup until restoration and binding are
complete. The resulting setup flow must respect the execution boundary above.
Cancel removes only staging owned by the operation. A partial folder is never ready.

rules.title: Progress and interfaces
rules.statement:
Extend the existing derived sync state. Cloud UI and CLI/API expose the same data:

- The project-folder boundary, applied `.pstignore`, excluded paths/rules, source
  device, audience and Git dependencies.
- Last completed capture, its interval and counts, plus files and bytes pending since.
- Per-entry read, transfer, quota, integrity or metadata problems, with an action needed.
- Separate progress for records, folder upload, local download and restoration.

A record download cannot imply that folder bytes are complete. Show a previous
completed copy alongside newer pending work. Count `.pstignore` exclusions separately
from the included-file denominator. Credentials, size limits and errors never silently
remove an included file. Offline restoration is
ready only when every required entry is available locally. Records remain usable
without a folder.

Core owns scanning, manifests, transfer, authorization and restoration. The public
SDK/API supports inspection, capture, source listing, download, restore, cancellation
and progress. CLI commands use the same methods; the Cloud extension owns its UI.
Keep additions next to released folder APIs and follow extension API deprecation
rules; do not silently change the existing `clone` input contract.

rules.title: R1 · Every device keeps a full local copy of every cloud project it can access and of   its user's private project
rules.statement:
Every device keeps a full local copy of every cloud project it can access and of
  its user's private project data, including file contents. It works fully offline.
  Append-only logs load bounded pages on demand under R60; a partial reader cannot
  publish a replacement that claims to contain history it has not downloaded.

rules.title: R2 · Plain record fields apply in relay order
rules.statement:
Plain record fields apply in relay order. The later ordered write wins at each
  changed JSON path. Objects contribute changed fields at every depth; arrays and
  undeclared strings, including multiline strings, are whole values. A replacement
  uses the caller's observed baseline to identify changed paths. Explicit set/unset
  paths state the author's intent directly. Neither clocks nor the relay interpret
  values.
  - A save is unconditional unless it supplies an expected revision. An earlier
    overlapping write, deletion/recreation, or change back to the original bytes
    refuses that entire conditional group on every device. Unrelated sibling changes
    do not refuse it. The originating extension can read the exact refused outcome.
  - Authors declare collaborative text by record prefix and JSON Pointer. Those
    fields merge typing with Yjs in the record stream. Real editable files retain
    their native text owner. A line break never declares text.
  - Plain sets use maps keyed by member; hand-arranged items use stable records and
    positions. Legacy shared maps/lists are deprecated, with maintained callers
    migrated to ordinary fields. The compatibility shared-text API remains explicit
    text until its coordinated removal.
  - Before the first Cloud join, saves settle in a durable local order and their envelopes
    are dropped. An empty relay is founded from local canonical state. When a stream
    already exists, local records become new unconditional saves after adoption; their
    pre-join conditions are not checked against remote history again. After joining,
    immutable pending saves overlay canonical records locally and survive restarts,
    adoption and uncertain acknowledgments. Exact per-epoch receipts settle them.
    Receipt roots use bounded encrypted index pages; a writer frontier is not proof
    that a save was accepted. See [ADR 0137](../adrs/0137-order-record-saves-and-declare-collaborative-text.md).

rules.title: R3 · The relay is never the source of truth
rules.statement:
The relay is never the source of truth. If the relay loses its data, a device
  with a full copy can upload it again. Its founding state establishes the new order;
  other devices adopt that base and replay their unsettled immutable saves. Exact
  known old outcomes settle a restored save before replay.

rules.title: R4 · A change that writes several records or files together is delivered and applied   as one unit on every client
rules.statement:
A change that writes several records or files together is delivered and applied
  as one unit on every client. A client never shows half of it. One save of an extension's
  records is one update in its record stream.

rules.title: R5 · Merging cannot keep rules that span records, such as "only one ticket is in   progress"
rules.statement:
Merging cannot keep rules that span records, such as "only one ticket is in
  progress". Two offline edits can break such a rule, and the extension shows or repairs
  the result. Unique resource numbers, record IDs and hand-arranged order do not fall
  under this rule: core provides them (R49 to R51).

rules.title: R6 · A save is durable on the local device before the product reports it as saved.
rules.statement: A save is durable on the local device before the product reports it as saved.

rules.title: R7 · The product shows the sync state of a cloud project: saved locally, waiting to   sync, synced, offline, or a p
rules.statement:
The product shows the sync state of a cloud project: saved locally, waiting to
  sync, synced, offline, or a problem that needs attention. Offline means the device has
  lost its connection. A project that does not sync is called Local, not Offline.

rules.title: R60 · Authors declare append-only project or device logs
rules.statement:
Authors declare append-only project or device logs. Project entries follow relay
  order; a device log has one writer and a logical read merges device streams. Reads
  and follow use bounded opaque cursors. Retention metadata excludes expired payloads
  before download. Appending one entry or reading the newest page at 100,000 entries
  must cost about the same as at 10 entries. New devices fetch only displayed pages.
  Personal-history indexes and completed transcript files use this generic transport;
  live/private session ownership, account isolation and terminal publication fences
  remain unchanged. Logs do not create local execution records on a receiving device.

rules.title: R49 · Core owns the number of every resource whose kind declares a prefix, such as   PS-12 or RP-4
rules.statement:
Core owns the number of every resource whose kind declares a prefix, such as
  PS-12 or RP-4. `resources.allocate` hands out numbers on each device. When two devices
  hand out the same number offline, core keeps it on the resource whose ID sorts first
  and gives the other the next free number. The rule uses IDs, not clocks. The old
  number stays an alias, so links, branch names and agent references still open the
  resource; an alias shared by two resources shows both. Extensions read the current
  number from core and do not keep their own copy.

rules.title: R50 · Extensions create record IDs with a core function
rules.statement:
Extensions create record IDs with a core function. Outside a data migration it
  returns a new random ID. Inside a data migration it derives the ID from the migration
  version and a key the extension passes, such as the ID of the source record, so two
  devices that run the same migration create the same records.

rules.title: R51 · Core provides order positions for lists that people arrange by hand
rules.statement:
Core provides order positions for lists that people arrange by hand. A position
  can be created between any two others, is unique to the device that created it, and
  never needs rebalancing. Two devices that move items at the same time end with the
  same order, with every item once.

rules.statement:
The SDK lets extension authors test their data on two simulated devices that edit
  offline and then merge. It reports which concurrent edits replaced each other.

rules.statement:
The relay sees only what it needs to route and store data: project ID, document
  ID, owner of private project data, sending device, sizes, times, update IDs, sequence numbers
  and blob IDs. Document and blob IDs are random and do not reveal names or content.

rules.statement:
Logs and error reports from the relay and the account manager contain no project

rules.title: R12 · Encryption keys come from the account manager after Google login
rules.statement:
Encryption keys come from the account manager after Google login. The relay
  never holds keys. The account manager and the relay are separate services with
  separate storage. Known limit: someone who controls both services can read data. A
  stronger key design, for example with passkeys, may replace this later.
