rules.title: R13 · Each cloud project has a project key that all members' devices get
rules.statement:
Each cloud project has a project key that all members' devices get. Each user's private
  project data has its own key that only that user's devices get.

rules.title: R14 · The account manager backs up keys separately from relay data
rules.statement:
The account manager backs up keys separately from relay data. Losing the key

rules.title: R15 · Removing a member or device creates a new key for future data
rules.statement:
Removing a member or device creates a new key for future data. Remaining devices
  keep the older keys so they can still read older data.

rules.title: R16 · A cloud device holds keys like any other device
rules.statement:
A cloud device holds keys like any other device. If the operator runs cloud
  devices and the relay, that operator can read the data of users with cloud devices.

rules.title: R17 · For each document, the relay keeps one latest state and the updates sent after   it
rules.statement:
For each document, the relay keeps one latest state and the updates sent after
  it. Together these are the sync source for offline devices and the cloud backup.

rules.title: R18 · When the updates after a latest state pass a size limit, an online device that   has all of them uploads a new
rules.statement:
When the updates after a latest state pass a size limit, an online device that
  has all of them uploads a new latest state. It names the latest state it was built on
  and the last update it includes. The relay accepts it only if it was built on the
  current latest state, so two devices cannot replace each other's work.

rules.title: R19 · Each latest state carries an encrypted summary of which edits it contains
rules.statement:
Each latest state carries an encrypted summary of which edits it contains. A
  client compares the summary with its own copy and sends any edits that are missing.
  An incomplete latest state cannot remove data that a device still holds.

rules.title: R20 · The relay keeps the previous latest state and the blobs it uses for a grace   period after a new one arrives
rules.statement:
The relay keeps the previous latest state and the blobs it uses for a grace
  period after a new one arrives. This protects against a broken upload. It is not

  quota or free-space reserve. If space cannot hold three snapshots, keep only the
  12-hour snapshot. A project, or one extension's data in it, can be restored to a
  snapshot through the CLI and API. The app has no restore screen (decided

  was decided on 2026-10-22 and replaces daily snapshots retained for 30 days.

  no inherited policy creates a missing `.pstignore` with `node_modules/`; never
  overwrite an existing policy or recreate one the user later deletes. Restored
  captures inherit their policy, including deliberate absence. Empty or deleted
  policies include all files.
  `.env`, keys, hidden and Git-ignored files, local extension code and `.pstdio` data
  are included unless users add matching rules. Always sync `.pstignore` itself.
  Show exclusions and matching rules separately from pending or blocked files.
  Unreadable, unsupported, changing or quota-blocked included entries keep the copy incomplete.
  Symlinks retain their target text without following it outside the folder. Capture
  required external Git administration explicitly when a worktree needs it, bounded
  by the owning repository's already registered canonical roots. Project pointers
  alone do not authorize reading unrelated local directories.

rules.title: Non-goals
rules.statement:
- Conflict screens or keeping both versions of a shared CRDT edit. Clients merge those
  edits; independent per-device folder captures follow R59.
- Version history on the relay.
- Queued commands for offline devices.
- Moving a running session to another device.
- Live source-file collaboration and moving terminal or process execution. Files in
  project folders, including credentials and caches, are covered by R57–R59.
- Protecting data from someone who controls both the account manager and the relay.
- Old-client compatibility, history migration or backfill. Alpha relay data has no
  users.

rules.title: Acceptance
rules.statement:
Phase 1 is done when:

- One user works on one cloud project from three devices, offline and online. Every
  device ends with the same content for Notes, Artifacts, Planner and an unrelated
  extension. No extension source contains sync, merge or encryption code.
- Two devices edit the same note, and different fields, nested keys and list items of
  one record, offline. Every edit survives the merge.
- Two devices create resources of the same kind offline. After the merge every resource
  has a unique number, the same on both devices, and its old number still opens it.
- Two devices run the same data migration offline and end with the same records.
- Two devices move the same cards offline and end with the same order, each card once.
- A multi-record change appears completely or not at all on every device.
- A device that missed several latest-state replacements catches up and keeps its own
  offline edits.
- A device that is offline when a new latest state is uploaded later restores any of
  its edits the latest state is missing.
- A test dump of the relay database and object storage, searched for known titles, file
  names, record text and file bytes from the test project, finds none of them.
- A reset device recovers every cloud project after Google login.
- A new device restores the project-folder contents included by `.pstignore` without
  a Git host, including `.env` and other Git-ignored files. The starter policy excludes
  `node_modules/`; custom exclusions, negation and policy changes behave as documented.
  Unsupported or missing included entries prevent a complete status. Only the owner's devices can decrypt
  folder captures, and existing destination work is preserved (R57–R59).
- An account without early access can log in, gets no cloud projects and sees Cloud
  sync as coming soon. An account with early access gets the full Cloud UI.
- A project made local is edited on two devices and then synced again. Both devices end
  with the same merged content.
- The Cloud status bar item, popover and Cloud settings come from the Prompt Studio
  Cloud extension. The dashboard ships no Cloud UI.
- After 10,000 edits to one project, relay storage for each document is below twice its
  latest state size plus the grace-period copy.
- A blob referenced by an offline edit is still available when that edit syncs within
  the grace period.
- The reference workload stays under the hosting target: one user, two cloud projects,
  three devices, 10,000 records and 5 GiB of files including one 1 GiB file, with a
  second account syncing during the large transfer.

Phases 2 and 3 get their own acceptance in their tickets.

rules.title: Decisions made during ticket refinement
rules.statement:
These defaults were chosen on 2026-10-19 so the phase tickets could be refined. The owner can change them.

- A record deleted on one device while another device edits it stays deleted.
- Core renumbers duplicate resource numbers after offline edits (R49). The resource whose ID sorts first keeps the number, and the other gets the next free number and keeps the old one as an alias. Planner and Reports only read the current number from core.
- The grace period for previous latest states and unused blobs is 7 days, set by the operator.
- A device uploads a new latest state when the updates after the current one exceed 1 MiB or 1,000 updates.
- A cloud project's data downloads without a local folder. Opening the project waits for download readiness, automatically attaches a managed local folder, and restores notes and declared artifact files. Existing local bindings are preserved. Setup shows progress and failures can be retried. This does not require Git or clone the project's source repository.
- Cloud devices run in the user's own cloud account from the released runtime image. Prompt Studio does not host or bill them in phase 2.

rules.title: Decisions made on 2026-10-21
rules.statement:
These came from the Cloud and Workspaces design review. The designs are in PR #1298 (`design/prompt-studio-design-system.pen`).

- The Cloud UI moves out of core into a bundled Prompt Studio Cloud extension (R55, R56). PS-784 now covers only the SDK and host side; PS-875 builds the extension.
- Early access comes before plans and billing (R54, PS-871).
- Offline means the connection is lost. Local means the project does not sync (R7).
- The Cloud popover has no sync switch. Making a project local is account-wide and lives in Cloud settings (R35).
- The popover lists devices only while the project syncs and the device is online.
- A project records its git remote when it becomes a cloud project, so a new device can offer to clone it when it first needs files (R34, PS-825).
- A bundled Workspaces extension shows the user's workspaces grouped by the device they live on, using the private project data from R38 (PS-876).
- "Personal space" is now called "private project data" in the product, docs and tickets. A new machine gets its cloud projects back in phase 1 (PS-825); private project data comes back in phase 2 (PS-826).

rules.title: Decisions made on 2026-10-30
rules.statement:
- Project-folder sync uses a separate root `.pstignore`, independent of `.gitignore`.
  The starter file excludes `node_modules/`. `.env` files remain included unless users
  add a rule. Users control further exclusions in that file. R57–R59 replace the earlier
  working-tree exclusion and the narrower coverage proposed during PS-960 refinement.
- Whole-folder captures are private to the source user's devices because they can
  contain credentials and private workspaces. Existing shared records and declared
  files retain their shared owners.
- Restore from the stored folder copy is the general new-device path. Clone and
  attach remain explicit alternatives. Live collaboration on source files is not part of this
  first recovery outcome. This is planned behavior, not a claim that it is shipped.

rules.title: Purpose
rules.statement:
1. Prompt Studio exists so that anyone who can direct an agent can build the tools they want and make their own work easier.
2. Tools share the same plumbing instead of rebuilding it. What one tool produces, another can use.
3. Check every feature, fix, and trade-off against this mission. A change that ships today must not block where the product is headed.

rules.title: Who Prompt Studio is for
rules.statement:
1. Anyone who can describe what they want. A person who never reads code must be able to build, run, change, and trust their tools.
2. A feature that only makes sense to someone who codes is not finished.

rules.title: What belongs in core
rules.statement:
1. Prompt Studio provides infrastructure every tool needs and no tool should build for itself. Everything else is an extension.
2. Agents and where they work: sessions, workspaces, and the machines work runs on.
3. The extension platform: installing, enabling, and running the tools people build.
4. UI contracts: the workbench, its layout, and how tools appear in it.
5. State and storage: what tools persist and where it lives.
6. Live sync: every client and agent seeing the same state.
7. Security and trust: keeping secrets away from tools and limiting what a tool may touch.
8. User attention: notifications and what may interrupt a person.
9. This list is closed. Extending it requires a human decision and an edit to this document.
10. A feature enters core only when extensions cannot build it or most extensions need it. One tool wanting it is not enough, even when core could ship it faster.

4. Whatever a person can do, an agent can do through the same interface with the same permissions, and the reverse.

4. Check whether an agent can drive it end to end.
5. Check whether it makes any direction in section 5 harder.

rules.title: Performance
rules.statement:
1. **Cold start: ≤2 seconds** on Apple M5 (10 CPU cores, 32 GiB RAM), from desktop process launch to an interactive workbench with the core API and default tools ready. Start with an empty app home and no app-owned processes running.
2. **Average memory: ≤2 GB** across all app-owned processes on the M5 reference machine. On macOS, use physical footprint, including compressed memory. The user selected 2 GB for these mandatory targets, replacing the former 1 GB advisory ceiling.
3. Memory workload: one local project, default extensions, a completed 100-message conversation, one open file, and one idle terminal. Measure 10 minutes of repeated opening and closing of the conversation, file, and panels after a 30-second settle.
4. **Idle renderer work: ≤2% script time and ≤5% task time** per renderer main thread over 10 seconds after a 2-second settle. These are shares of elapsed time, not whole-app CPU usage.

2. Agents **SHOULD** run relevant local benchmarks for changes with significant performance impact. Ordinary changes can rely on nightly coverage.

Use the [M5 and memory reference procedure](../guides/development/0016-writing-benchmarks.md#m5-and-average-memory-reference-procedure) for sampling, [writing benchmarks](../guides/development/0016-writing-benchmarks.md) for commands, and [CI stages](../guides/development/0015-ci-stages.md#nightly-full-validation) for the schedule.

5. Do not create extension data folders directly under `.pstdio/` or keep runtime data in extension source folders. `.pstdio/extensions/` holds extension source.
6. Files an extension deliberately edits as project source, such as icon fonts, stay at their configured paths. The extension's own settings and working files stay in extension storage.

rules.title: 1. Outcome
rules.statement:
People can open a website or local development server beside their work, select an element on the page, and attach useful context to a conversation without manually describing where it is. The same selection interaction works inside UI Canvas. Extensions can consume the result for their own inspectors, tickets, reports, or editing workflows.

The browser is an extension built on public host capabilities. Core provides the browser surface, device ownership, permission checks, and shared attachment integration. A small DOM inspection package provides highlighting and element descriptions independently of the browser, Canvas, or chat.

This document proposes product behavior and an architecture to validate. Proposed API names and package locations are illustrative. They are not supported contracts or accepted architecture decisions. The design previews use synthetic content; they do not embed an external site or prove Electron composition.

rules.title: Goals
rules.statement:
1. Browse an HTTP or HTTPS page inside a normal workbench panel on desktop.
2. Preserve the live page across tab changes, panel hiding, and supported panel moves.
3. Select an element in either a browser page or a Canvas example with the same interaction and result model.
4. Review selected context before adding it to a specific conversation draft.
5. Let people and agents use the same authorized operations against an explicit surface.
6. Keep website content separate from the application's authentication, extension capabilities, and privileged APIs.
7. Make the first implementation small enough to validate without introducing a second browser distribution or a new layout engine.

rules.title: 4. Product ownership and mission fit
rules.statement:
This supports the mission by letting a person show an agent the exact part of a tool they want to change. It removes the need to understand DOM selectors or manually assemble debugging evidence.

| Owner | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Browser extension | Browser resources, saved destinations, entry commands, project/workspace associations, and workflow-specific actions. |
| Workbench | Tabs, panel location, pinning, focus, visibility, region sizing, and resource/view identity. |
| Core browser surface and device service | Live browser handles, platform driver admission, native placement, session isolation, and authorized operations. |
| Shared DOM inspection package | Pointer/keyboard selection, highlight rendering, bounded element description, and cleanup. |
| Canvas package and extension | Frame lifecycle, preview identity, frame transport, coordinate mapping, and Canvas-specific source context. |
| Session draft owner | Draft text, attachment references, deduplication, removal, and submission. |
| Other extensions | Their own use of inspection results, storage, and actions. |

The browser workflow belongs in an extension. Hosting native content requires privileged infrastructure an extension cannot implement by itself; that belongs in core's UI and trust contracts. The built-in browser must use the same public interface available to external extensions. This follows mission rules `001.3.4`, `001.3.7`, `001.3.10`, `001.4.2`, and `001.4.4`.

rules.title: Scenario: Agent and person inspect the same live page
rules.statement:
> **Given** an authorized agent and a browser session on a named device, **When** the agent requests element context, **Then** it receives data from that session's current document and the person can see which page is being used.

An unavailable device or closed session produces a specific error. The operation never silently moves to another browser or creates a headless replacement.

rules.title: Scenario: Recover from navigation, a rebuild, or capture failure
rules.statement:
> **Given** a pending selection or screenshot, **When** the page navigates or the Canvas frame rebuilds, **Then** the pending result is cancelled or rejected as stale.

A completed context snapshot remains readable after navigation. A failed screenshot leaves the text context available with a visible explanation. A crashed page offers Reload; recovery does not claim to preserve lost form state.

rules.title: Browser panel
rules.statement:
| ID | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| B1 | Use normal Main, Side, or Secondary panel placement and existing resource tabs. Do not nest a competing tab strip inside the browser body. |
| B2 | Keep browser controls above the page viewport; page scrolling must not move the controls. |
| B3 | Show the committed URL, title, loading state, navigation availability, and actionable load failure. Distinguish a typed destination from a successfully loaded one. |
| B4 | Support HTTP/HTTPS navigation and a host-controlled empty state. Opening unsupported protocols follows an explicit external-link policy. |
| B5 | Bind a live guest to an opaque session handle, not to its URL. Redirects must not change tab identity. |
| B6 | Preserve the guest when the panel is hidden or moved. Explicit close, project disposal, and device shutdown release its resources. |
| B7 | Restore focus between address field, page, panel navigation, and inspection controls. Standard workbench shortcuts remain reachable while the page has focus. |
| B8 | Route popup/new-window requests through host policy. Initial delivery must handle them visibly, even when an authentication flow requires the system browser. |
| B9 | Use an isolated, device-local browsing partition per project for the initial profile. Provide Clear browsing data. Do not reuse the workbench partition. |
| B10 | Explain unsupported client capabilities inline and offer Open externally when appropriate. |

rules.title: Element selection
rules.statement:
| ID | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| E1 | Inspect is an explicit mode. Normal page behavior resumes on selection, cancellation, navigation, or disposal. |
| E2 | Highlight the hovered target without changing application layout. Exclude inspector-owned elements from hit testing and serialization. |
| E3 | Support pointer selection and a keyboard path to choosing a focused target, confirming, and cancelling. The exact target-traversal interaction is a design validation item. |
| E4 | Produce useful DOM context without React or other framework metadata. Optional enrichers may add information but cannot block the base result indefinitely. |
| E5 | Bind every live request to the project, device/surface, document generation, frame, and request ID. Reject responses from replaced documents. |
| E6 | Treat locator candidates as hints. A later operation must re-resolve them and fail on a missing or ambiguous match. |
| E7 | Bound text, HTML, styles, depth, and total payload size. Omit password values, hidden form values, scripts, and unrelated document content. |
| E8 | Present unavailable component source, inaccessible child frames, and missing screenshots as explicit limitations. Do not manufacture metadata. |
| E9 | Keep hover, current target, and active inspection mode local and transient. Persist only an explicitly accepted context snapshot. |

rules.title: Context attachment
rules.statement:
| ID | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | Review identifies the source page or Canvas frame and the destination conversation before attachment. |
| A2 | Attach appends context to the existing draft and never submits the conversation. It preserves text and existing attachments. |
| A3 | Capture the draft identity when the action starts. A later focus change must not redirect the attachment. |
| A4 | Use an idempotency key for attachment insertion. Retrying after an uncertain reply must not duplicate the same context. |
| A5 | Store images and large serialized evidence through existing file/blob APIs. Draft records hold small metadata and references. |
| A6 | Removing an unsent attachment follows existing reference and cleanup rules. Sent evidence remains available in the conversation history. |
| A7 | Keep selected page content clearly identified as evidence supplied by the page. It must not become privileged agent instructions. |

rules.title: 9. Canvas integration
rules.statement:
1. Mount the shared inspector inside the existing frame runtime. Keep the iframe's opaque sandbox and current parent/source checks.
2. Extend the typed frame protocol with inspection requests and results. Negotiate support so an older built frame reports unavailable instead of hanging.
3. Give Inspect to the selected frame. Escape first cancels inspection; it must not also clear the Canvas frame selection or trigger an unrelated workbench action.
4. Preserve the existing pan/zoom controls, frame theme, parameter editing, and reset behavior.
5. Add visibility propagation from the outer extension webview into nested frames. Visible frames may inspect; hidden frames suspend inspector and owned measurement work while retaining component state.
6. On rebuild/reset, advance document identity, cancel pending operations, remove overlays/listeners, and reconnect after the replacement frame is ready.
7. Use the same result review and attachment action as browser selection. Canvas supplies additional provenance through the adapter.

Existing entry points are [frame runtime](../../packages/canvas/src/runtime/frame-runtime.tsx), [frame protocol](../../packages/canvas/src/runtime/protocol.ts), [frame host](../../extensions/canvas/src/frames/frame.tsx), [frame geometry](../../extensions/canvas/src/controller/frame-bounds.ts), and [startup scheduling](../../extensions/canvas/src/frames/use-frame-startup.ts).

rules.title: 10. Public API and agent behavior
rules.statement:
The new API must be additive and versioned under the [extension API compatibility rules](book.json). Declare the minimum supported host API version and expose unsupported capabilities before a caller starts an operation.

| Operation family | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Discover | List accessible browser sessions and inspectable surfaces with device, owner, readiness, and supported operations. |
| Browser lifecycle | Open, navigate, reload, back/forward, close, and read current status against an explicit target. |
| Inspect | Start/cancel human selection; describe a target or enumerate a bounded set of candidate elements for an agent; return the same result model. |
| Capture | Request a current viewport or selected-element capture when the target driver supports it. |
| Attach context | Append a reviewed result and optional files to a named conversation draft; return the resulting attachment identity. |

Interactive selection cannot be the only way agents obtain context. Agents need a non-interactive description operation and bounded discovery so they can identify a target without guessing an opaque selector. Surface ownership and permissions apply equally to UI, CLI, and agent requests.

Expose browser extension actions through `cli: true` commands. Route device operations through the host, with cancellation and typed errors such as unsupported capability, unavailable device, closed session, stale document, ambiguous target, and capture unavailable. Final names belong in implementation tickets.

The picker never sends a prompt. A separate consumer may create a session or follow up through existing APIs when the user explicitly chooses that action. Draft attachment requires a new public integration with the current draft owner; the existing create/follow-up methods are not a substitute.

rules.title: 11. Lifecycle, storage, and synchronization
rules.statement:
| Event | Required transition |
| --- | --- |
| Panel becomes hidden | Retain its document, stop inspection input, and suspend unnecessary owned work. |
| Panel moves | Update presentation; keep the same browser handle and live document. |
| Main-document navigation begins | Cancel active selection and mark pending captures stale; advance document generation. |
| Canvas rebuild/reset | Release the previous frame connection and all live element handles. |
| Capture starts | Acquire a bounded rendering lease if the driver needs painting; never steal foreground focus solely to capture. |
| Capture completes/fails/cancels | Release the lease and restore the prior presentation policy. |
| Browser crashes | Report failure, invalidate handles, and offer explicit reload. |
| Owner closes or project switches | Cancel requests, release control and capture leases, then dispose native guests and listeners. |
| Device disconnects | Fail pending calls. Do not queue browser mutations for an unknown later page. |
| Result is attached | Preserve an immutable context snapshot and file references independently of the live page. |

Persist only data needed for deliberate restoration: browser resource identity, saved destination and extension-owned preferences. Workbench layout remains authoritative for tab order and placement. Cookies and site storage remain device-local inside the browser partition. Do not synchronize cookies, native handles, navigation stacks, live DOM handles, hover state, or control claims as project records.

Use extension storage for extension data, and existing session attachment storage for conversation evidence. Respect the 256 KiB record and 4 MiB record-commit limits. Establish smaller inspector-specific limits before implementation; truncation must be explicit rather than silently splitting one large result across records.

rules.title: 12. Capture and attachment details
rules.statement:
Desktop browser capture uses the guest's capture capability. Desktop Canvas capture needs a host-owned frame-to-window geometry path; the guest cannot request an arbitrary screen rectangle. Capture only the intended application surface and validate the document/layout revision before and after capture.

Convert CSS coordinates, frame offsets, Canvas zoom, desktop zoom, scroll, and device scale exactly once in the owning adapter. Clip the crop to the viewport. Partly offscreen elements receive a visible-region capture or an explicit limitation; initial delivery does not scroll the page automatically to assemble a full-element image.

Selection works without capture. Web-hosted Canvas must not promise exact screenshots from an iframe using DOM serialization. A later consented display-capture or remote-browser feature can provide that capability separately.

Attach uses the current draft service and existing file upload path. It must preserve drafts when upload or insertion fails, avoid orphaning files on cancellation, and allow retry without duplication. Display the source, selection summary, and capture availability in the attachment preview. The final model-facing representation includes source provenance and bounded element data; it does not embed hidden page instructions as system text.

rules.title: 13. Security and privacy requirements
rules.statement:
- Keep website sessions separate from workbench credentials, cookies, custom protocols, and preload APIs.
- Keep sandboxing, context isolation, and web security enabled. Disable Node integration in guests and subframes.
- Validate URL schemes, redirects, popup policy, permission requests, and download behavior at the host boundary.
- Do not expose raw Electron objects, CDP endpoints, unrestricted JavaScript evaluation, or arbitrary host IPC through the public browser API.
- Bind operations to authenticated callers, project access, allowed capabilities, target device, and the live surface owner.
- Validate and size-limit messages from inspected documents. Never resolve a page-supplied source path as a workspace file without normal workspace checks.
- Capture only after a deliberate request. Do not continuously screenshot or serialize pages in the background.
- Avoid storing page text, DOM payloads, screenshots, or credential-bearing URLs in diagnostic logs. Record operation IDs and bounded failure categories instead.
- Screenshot review must make clear that visible page content can include sensitive information; the user can remove the image before attachment.

rules.title: 14. Performance and accessibility
rules.statement:
The [mandatory nonfunctional targets](book.json) remain unchanged: core download and binary at most 200 MB each, cold start at most 2 seconds on the specified M5 machine, average app-owned memory at most 2 GB in the defined workload, and the stated idle-renderer limits.

Desktop reuses its bundled Chromium. Browser resources and inspector code load on demand. No browser guest starts merely because the extension is installed. Shared inspector code must not import the application UI framework into every target page. Use a small overlay implementation with a host-supplied theme contract.

Do not poll the DOM continuously. Track hover at most once per animation frame while inspecting, observe only what is needed, and release observers/listeners at the end. Keep optional framework enrichment off the hover path. Measure realistic workloads with multiple retained Canvas frames and a hidden browser in addition to the existing mandatory workload.

All controls have accessible names and visible keyboard focus. Inspect can be cancelled without a pointer. Announce selection and capture failures through the relevant accessible status region. Highlighting uses more than color alone. Keyboard traversal and screen-reader behavior need an integrated validation pass before release.

rules.title: Critical acceptance checks
rules.statement:
1. Open two destinations, type into a form, move/hide/show a panel, and verify the same document and input remain.
2. Open a command palette and modal over a browser surface; all controls remain visible and focusable.
3. Pick a link or button; its ordinary action does not execute during selection. Escape restores normal interaction.
4. Inspect a Canvas frame at multiple zoom levels and after scrolling; highlight and capture coordinates agree.
5. Rebuild or navigate during enrichment/capture; no result from the old document reaches the new selection or draft.
6. Fail optional source enrichment and screenshot capture; bounded DOM context remains usable.
7. Attach twice with the same request identity; exactly one draft item appears and no message is sent.
8. Attempt an operation from another project, stale frame, or unauthorized device; the host rejects it.
9. Close the resource/window and disconnect the caller; no guest, listener, control claim, or capture lease remains owned by the closed session.
10. Run the same public operations through an external test extension and agent command path.
11. Verify installed-package inclusion for the inspector/preload and capability-version behavior with an older unsupported host/frame.
12. Confirm browser guests are absent from cold start until opened and hidden inspection does not introduce ongoing renderer work.

Implementation tests should target behavior at the lowest useful layer, with focused real-browser/Electron checks for the native and isolation boundaries. Follow [testing guidance](../guidance/0005-testing.md). This proposal records no implementation test or benchmark results.

rules.title: Parameter editor
rules.statement:
1. Keep bounded values on one line with their label: IDs, timestamps, status, and other single choices.
2. Put growing values below their label: dependencies, blocked reasons, review links, multi-value fields, and multiline content. Let the value area wrap as needed.
3. Keep dropdown triggers within their parent width and dropdown menus within the available viewport. Long selected values and options must truncate without pushing controls outside their container.
4. Omit the Review links row when there are no links.

rules.title: Conversion safety acceptance (historical release gate)
rules.statement:
This proposed gate was written for the historical 0.45 conversion. Reconcile its timing and mechanisms with the current storage contract before implementation; preserve its safety conditions rather than assuming the conversion passed them.

The conversion moves blob and file-ID bytes into assets and collection records into domain records.
It cannot merge until all of these hold:

- This PRD lists the default limits, free-space reserve and protected-data rules, with the
  measurement run they come from.
- A test converts a fixture project, records peak disk use during conversion, and shows that
  conversion refuses to start, with the space needed, when free space is below that peak plus the
  reserve.
- A test interrupts conversion at each durable boundary, restarts, and finishes without duplicate
  records or assets and without deleting source data before verification.
- A test exhausts space during staging and during a local save. Saved work survives, no group is
  half-applied and the caller gets the capacity outcome.
- A test stores 100 distinct 10 MB versions and repeated identical uploads, and reports asset bytes,
  database growth, editable copies and temporary peaks separately.
- After conversion, eviction and compaction stay off: completed asset versions and journal entries
  remain, and the assets guide still matches.

rules.title: Public storage transition and deprecation boundary
rules.statement:
`storage.records` and `storage.assets` shipped in 0.44 with behavior this PRD removes.
Under API versioning, changing
documented runtime behavior is a breaking change. Plan it as one breaking step:

| Member | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `records.read`, `records.list`, `records.id` | Keep. `read` loses its `branch` argument. |
| `records.commit` | Keep as the write call. Optional `expectedRevision` makes the group conditional; plain changes otherwise apply in relay order (R2). |
| `StorageSaveOutcome` | Report the R7 states. Remove `conflict` and the relay checkpoint. |
| `records.outcome` | Keep. It returns the R7 save states, so a caller can wait until a save has synced. |
| `records.conflicts`, `records.inspect`, `records.resolve` | Deprecate, then remove. There are no conflicts to inspect. |
| `storage.assets` retained versions and unresolved alternatives | Remove from the documented behavior. |

Add the new shapes next to the old ones, mark the old ones `@deprecated` with their
replacement, and remove them together in the next breaking release.

The core functions from R49 to R52 are additions that do not break existing extensions:
`storage.ids.create()`, `migration.id(key)` inside `storage.migrate`,
`storage.positions.between()`, `resources.identity()`, `resources.findByShorthand()`,
the `resourceEvents.renumbered` event, and the SDK's two-device test helper.
